title: Invocation is a 3-tuple — .0/.1/.2 indexing all over jmap-server is primitive-obsession at the foundation type level
description: Invocation is a type alias '(String, Value, String)' in jmap-types representing (method_name, args, call_id). jmap-server indexes it as .0/.1/.2 in 11+ sites: src/lib.rs:153, 209 (handler dispatch); src/parse.rs:163-165 (find prior_responses by call_id); src/response.rs:30 (error_invocation construction); plus test code throughout. Every use site has a comment of the form 'Invocation layout: (method_name, args, call_id) — RFC 8620 §3.3' because the tuple shape is otherwise opaque at the call site. Idiomatic Rust uses a named struct 'pub struct Invocation { method: String, args: Value, call_id: String }' so call sites read inv.method, inv.args, inv.call_id without explanatory comments. The current tuple shape is justified by JMAP wire serialization being a JSON triple [method, args, callId], but that is a Serialize/Deserialize concern (custom Serialize impl produces the array shape) — it does not require the in-memory Rust shape to be a tuple. What goes wrong if it stays: every new handler/dispatcher consumer must re-learn that .0=method, .1=args, .2=call_id; the workspace-wide AGENTS.md 'primitive obsession' rule for newtypes applies here at the slightly-larger-grained level of composite-tuple-vs-struct; refactoring Invocation later is a workspace-wide change because of the .0/.1/.2 indexing pattern is locked into every consumer. Note: this is a workspace-level change (Invocation lives in jmap-types), not a jmap-server-local one. Flag it here because jmap-server is the heaviest consumer; surface the workspace bead for the actual type-design discussion.
close_reason: Closed under the JMAP-6xs8.17 decision: Invocation is a named struct (df8926be). CI green at 8e240e18 (stable+beta 3502 passed).
